title: Auth middleware — verify JWT access token on protected routes
description: Create middleware that validates the JWT access token from the Authorization header and attaches the decoded user ID to the request. All protected routes use this middleware.
acceptanceCriteria: Middleware reads Bearer token from Authorization header
Returns 401 if token is missing, malformed, or expired
Protected routes return 401 without valid token

steps.details: Create server/src/middleware/requireAuth.ts. Extract token from req.headers.authorization ('Bearer TOKEN'). If missing, return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Authentication required' }). Call verifyAccessToken(token) — catch errors and return 401. Attach req.userId = decoded.sub. Call next().
Create server/src/types/express.d.ts: declare global { namespace Express { interface Request { userId: string; } } }. This avoids TypeScript errors when accessing req.userId.
In index.ts, apply requireAuth to all /api routes EXCEPT /api/auth/* and /api/share/*. Either use router-level middleware or apply selectively per router.
Call GET /api/users/me without token — expect 401. Call with valid token — expect 200. Call with expired token — expect 401.

technicalNotes: Access tokens expire in 15 minutes — the frontend must call /api/auth/refresh before they expire
Never check the database on every request — JWT is self-contained; use DB only for refresh tokens
